newsitem.title: USA: Selas expects 1997 to be better than 1996.
newsitem.headline: Selas expects 1997 to be better than 1996.

text.p: Selas Corp said Tuesday it expects 1997 to be a better year than 1996, which it described as exceptional.

The company cited improved performance from Resistance Technology Inc, strong backlog and sales activity in its heat technology group, and improved performance by Deuer Manufacturing, the subsidiary serving the automotive industry.

Selas, a diversified firm with international operations and sales that engage in making products like precision electronic components, reported net income for the first quarter of $0.33 per share, up from $0.17 a year earlier.
It said earnings would have been about $0.08 per share higher had it not been for "unfavorable" foreign currency exchange rates and a severe winter-related delay in hearing aid orders.
It said it expected to see the orders made up as the year progressed.
